notes.1-8: The extracts were short, straightforward interactions. Nearly all candidates answered Questions 1 , 5 and 8 successfully. A third of candidates were not familiar with manteau in Question 2 and chose écharpe instead . Similar numbers of candidates did not know raisin in Question 4 . In Question 6 , some candidates did not recognise serviette. In Question 7 , over a third of candidates did not know faire la vaisselle.
notes.9-14: Candidates heard a longer extract which featured an advertisement for an activity holiday in Biarritz. Overall, candidates performed well in this exercise. In Question 10 , some candidates did not understand forêt and often chose C ( lac ) instead . Question 12 was the most challenging with under two thirds of candidates correctly choosing option D , plongée.
notes.15-19: This was a matching exercise in which candidates heard a conversation between two friends about hotels in Switzerland. Overall candidates performed well in this exercise. Question 15 was attempted well. Three quarters of the cohort answered Question 16 correctly; those who answered incorrectly heard les chambres sont très spacieuses and chose C . Question 17 was the most challenging; just over half the candidates matched bon marché with pas cher and selected the correct option A . The most frequent incorrect answers were options C and D . Question 19 was attempted well and nearly three quarters of the candidates selected option D , with A being the most common error.
notes.20-28: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview in two parts with Mattis who talked about playing street golf in Paris. The exercise represented a step up in the incline of difficulty of the test. For Question 20 , almost two thirds of candidates chose the correct option C . Most of those who answered incorrectly chose distractor A . Similar numbers answered Question 21 successfully, whilst some candidates missed the imperfect tense ( au début, j’avais des difficultés ) and opted for distractor C . Over two thirds of candidates answered Question 22 correctly; most of those who answered incorrectly heard même en ville and chose distractor B . Question 23 was demanding and fewer than a third of candidates understood s’est mis en colère ; most chose distractor A . Question 24 was answered correctly by over two thirds of candidates. Those who answered incorrectly heard pour ne pas causer d’accident and wrongly linked accidents to the dogs, choosing distractor A . Most candidates successfully answered Question 25 . Question 26 was attempted well, with distractor A being the most common error. Many candidates also answered Question 27 correctly; some candidates heard rapide and missed the negative, incorrectly opting for distractor B. Question 28 proved the most challenging with just over a quarter of candidates matching ça ne coûte rien with gratuit . Most candidates heard populaire and incorrectly chose distractor B .
notes.29-34: Candidates heard an interview with Karim about a holiday in France. This was an appropriately demanding exercise at this stage of the paper. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French November 2021 Question 29 was the most challenging; only a few candidates understood on plantait notre tente dans des bois et des champs and chose option B . Most selected distractor A . Question 30 was successfully attempted by over half the candidates. Those who answered incorrectly chose distractors A and B . Question 31 was well attempted with over two thirds of candidates choosing the correct option D . There was no clear pattern of incorrect answers. Question 32 was demanding with under half the cohort choosing the correct option D ; many candidates missed le lendemain and incorrectly chose distractors A and B . Over half the candidates answered Question 33 correctly, with distractor A the most common error. Similar numbers of candidates answered Question 34 successfully. Those who answered incorrectly often heard d’autres régions à explorer and chose distractor D .
notes.35-37: In this exercise, candidates heard an interview with Camille about her life in Tahiti. For each question in this exercise, candidates had to identify two correct statements from a choice of five. This was an appropriately demanding and challenging exercise at this stage of the paper. Question 35 was attempted well by many candidates with about three quarters of the cohort selecting option B and over half correctly choosing option D . Some candidates chose distractor E ; they needed to listen carefully to what Camille said, as being bored did not refer to her work but to life on the island ( il faut travailler, sinon on s’ennuie ). Question 36 was demanding and only half the candidates correctly chose options A and D . Many heard certains touristes ne trouvent pas ça poli and incorrectly chose distractor E . For Question 37 over half the cohort successfully selected option B , and over a third chose option E . Many candidates misunderstood the time, sept heures et demie, and chose distractor D .
